paper.title: On the Limits of Language Generation: Trade-Offs Between Hallucination and Mode Collapse
paper.summary: Establishes statistical universal-rate boundaries for identification, fresh generation, and breadth. Lean proves full oracle-relative Theorems 3.1--3.3 with explicit computation boundaries, certified finite-case identification rates. Theorem 3.4 derives ordinary word-support decidability for every-tape-total encoded token machines, with auxiliary state and EOS explicit. Theorem 3.6 proves intended statistical unambiguous-generation impossibility with corrected failure loss and a stronger semantic lower bound. Theorem 3.8 proves the statistical approximate-breadth no-rate conclusion through support locking and finite tell-tales. Proposition 3.10 gives certified last-critical subset-oracle identification with exponential IID error and no tell-tale access. Propositions 3.11--3.12 now have certified membership-only computation, retaining the 3.12 proof repair. Theorem 3.13 proves optimal exponential labeled identification with deterministic correct labels, full marginal support, and a randomized fixed-law lower bound. Theorems 3.5, 3.7, and 3.9 now have full online PMF/MOP wrappers, bounded computable identification reductions, and explicit oracle/ordinary-computation boundaries. Theorem 3.5 realizes both output conventions; separate effective results use uniform MOP.

formalization_scope.summary: All thirteen Section 3 main result cards are fully covered in their documented models: infinite-language oracle sampling for the positive generation results, semantic/ConditionTwo identifiability for the source-facing boundaries, and explicit ordinary-computation specializations. Three appendix result cards remain uncovered and the aggregate definition card is partial. Theorem 3.5 now has fresh and repetition-allowing PMF constructions, certified support membership, and ordinary-MOP biconditionals under computable family membership. Theorems 3.7/3.9 retain source pointwise MOP via stronger semantic obstructions. Bounded identifiers stabilize to a fixed target index; separate effective impossibility/equivalence results explicitly use uniform MOP. Source loss/proof repairs remain documented.
specializations: SupportGenerator supplies a total Boolean membership answer for each support extensionally; it is not a Turing-machine code or a computability certificate.

The legacy Theorem 3.5 support-set construction is general. The canonical positive PMF construction uses infinite languages, certified membership/tell-tale training, and the same sampler as Theorem 3.3. Its ordinary pointwise MOP assumes computable membership; ordinary uniform sampling also assumes computable training.

FreshBreadthInLimit records eventual support K minus the observed sample, while RepeatingBreadthInLimit records eventual support K. Lean reunites the sample with fresh support before identification and separately proves the repetition-allowing negative reduction.

Theorems 3.7/3.9 now apply the stronger support-semantic obstructions to actual PMF kernels with pointwise DecidableMOP and StatisticalStable. The conclusion is online along every positive presentation; no IID-rate hypothesis or random-tape derandomization is used.
All native P03 endpoints use the natural-number encoding of the source's arbitrary countable domain.
Statistical samples are ordered IID lists from Mathlib PMFs on natural numbers. ValidDistribution requires support exactly equal to the target; error compares languages, permitting duplicate indices.

Theorem 3.1's lower-bound component quantifies over every semantic randomized kernel, hence also over computable randomized learners, and chooses one fixed valid distribution witnessing error at least exp(-2n) infinitely often.

Propositions 3.11--3.12 have one distribution-independent deterministic learner with distribution-dependent positive constants c,D satisfying error_n <= D exp(-c n) for every sample size. A fixed TruthTableProgram has primitive-recursive query formation and computable postprocessing; equality to finiteVersionSpaceLearner and ordinary computation under computable membership are proved.

Proposition 3.12 retains the source's statistical conclusion while replacing its incorrect least-consistent construction by the bounded version-space learner; this is a proof repair, not an extra finite-family assumption.

Theorem 3.1 uses nonnegative real-valued sublinear exponents tending to infinity, making the exponential rate [0,1]-valued and vanishing as required by Definition 13. No monotonicity or computability assumption on the exponent is added.
A stronger Angluin-stage-learner exponential upper bound supplies every required almost-exponential rate at horizontal scale one, with one learner independent of both exponent and distribution.

The positive computation witness is a TruthTableProgram: primitive recursive query formation and a Computable postprocessor. At sample size n it queries candidate indices at most n, tell-tale emission stages below n, and membership of observed points. No completion test is used.

The no-rate branch is proved directly using continuous finite-sample sequence laws and Baire category, for all randomized PMF kernels; the result includes limsup error at least one half under one fixed valid distribution. No Angluin-1988 theorem is assumed as an axiom.
Ordinary uniform computability is separately proved under P00A ConditionOne. The oracle-relative Theorem 3.1 does not identify nonuniform ConditionTwo with ordinary effective identification.

Theorem 3.2 explicitly uses infinite candidate languages, as required by the generation discussion on source page 2 and the proof of Lemma 5.10. Its strict fresh-output statistical loss does not adopt Definition 12's exhausted-finite-target exception.

GenerationNontrivial uses a finite subfamily with nonempty finite intersection, independently of the identification nontriviality predicate. The lower bound holds for every randomized PMF kernel, under one fixed target distribution for infinitely many sample sizes.

Lemma 5.13 gives P01's actual stateful membership-query KM machine finite witnesses and an exponential IID rate. The public certifiedKM is a stateless finite-critical search over encoded cutoff/candidate pairs; equality of outputs or running time with the source machine is not claimed.

Theorem 3.2 uses only uniform family membership. OracleSearchProgram certifies primitive recursive finite query stages and a computable postprocessor; P01 round termination proves a successful stage exists for every finite input. Computable membership gives ordinary uniform Computable certifiedKM.

Theorem 3.3 uses exact fresh support equality and an outer probability over the IID training sample. It does not replace support equality by single-output success or silently use repetition-allowing breadth.

DecidableMOP follows Definition 6: each trained generator has some computable support decider. UniformDecidableMOP additionally provides one procedure uniform in the sample. OracleMOP gives certified truth-table procedures relative to the standing membership oracle.

Lemma 6.4 proves a stronger semantic obstruction: for every PMF generator on a non-identifiable family, one fixed valid distribution has limsup breadth error at least one half. This uses Theorem 3.1's semantic necessity and therefore avoids extracting a uniform decider from pointwise MOP.

Proposition 6.5 is realized in the infinite-language generation regime by a full-support geometric natural seed followed by a terminating upward membership search. Seed x returns x whenever it is an unseen member, proving exact support equality.

The positive breadth branch uses Theorem 3.1's certified membership/tell-tale identifier. Each trained support has a membership-only oracle-MOP procedure. Computable membership gives ordinary pointwise MOP; computable membership and tell-tale enumeration give an ordinary computable seeded sampler and uniform MOP. An effective ConditionOne corollary is separately proved.

HasComputableSampler is a sufficient certificate for the constructed laws: a standard geometric seed and a total computable numerical map. It is not a universal characterization of computable PMFs and does not encode arbitrary randomized Turing-machine descriptions.

Theorem 3.4 uses computable encoded small-step transitions with halt, deterministic, and fair-bit actions. AlwaysHalts means termination on every input and every random tape, not merely almost surely. A compiler from literal TM syntax is not provided.

The random-tape interpreter pads deterministic steps. An actual-read execution relation and canOutput_iff_executes prove exact preservation of finite output support. Fair finite bit words give positive probability precisely to possible outputs.

Cantor compactness supplies a uniform finite execution bound per input, completing the printed Lemma 6.3 argument. An ordinary computable search finds a sufficient bound without advice and proves exact support membership; actual coin reads are bounded too.

Token support follows one compatible path of reachable auxiliary states and requires EOS after the queried tokens. EOS is excluded from the returned list as an encoding convention. Outer generation need not halt, so a finite word experiment defines support without assuming a normalized PMF over complete words.

wordSupport_has_code and randomized_support_has_code give finite partial-recursive code witnesses for fixed supplied computable machines. decidableMOP_of_token_support transfers the result to trained PMF families with exactly the encoded finite-word support; no normalized PMF is assumed for a nonterminating outer process.

Theorem 3.6 uses the existing UnambiguousAt strict extended-cardinality comparison on the trained PMF support and the existing online Stable predicate through statisticalSupportView. Repetitions of training examples are allowed. The outer probability is over ordered IID training samples.

The printed loss before Theorem 3.6 is a success indicator. unambiguousError is failure probability, printedUnambiguousError records the literal success probability, and their complement identity is proved. The intended theorem, not the literal reversed vanishing-loss objective, is formalized.

Strict unambiguity selects a unique extensional target. A classical closestSupportIdentifier has identification error bounded by unambiguous failure. It is not asserted computable from MOP; it is used only by the existing necessity theorem covering every semantic randomized identifier.

The stronger unambiguousError_frequently_ge_half and limsup theorem need neither stability nor MOP. Results.theorem_3_6 retains the source assumptions. Non-identifiability is the same semantic Angluin ConditionTwo boundary as Theorem 3.1, not merely ordinary effective non-identifiability when ConditionTwo holds.

NoUnambiguousRate gives one fixed valid distribution with positive limsup error. It excludes all vanishing natural-domain rates and all vanishing real-domain rates with distribution-dependent positive horizontal and vertical scales. No monotonicity or computability of a rate is required.

Theorem 3.6 uses an alternative direct finite-sample proof. Source Proposition 7.2 and Lemmas 7.3--7.4 are not duplicated, and no common deterministic random tape is extracted from separate probability-one claims for all presentations.

Theorem 3.8 reuses ApproximateBreadthAt and StatisticalStable unchanged. Its failure probability is exactly equation (6): support inconsistency or infinitely many omitted target points. Finite omissions and repetitions of training examples are allowed.

The generic Support.Locking theorem supplies a finite prefix fixing the entire support under every target-contained continuation. DiscreteSamplePrefix proves its positive IID mass is independent of continuation length, so a bad lock forces positive error limsup.

If all valid laws had nonpositive approximate-breadth limsup, the lock would approximate the target. Prefix contents, the finite omission set, and one target point form a tell-tale; any compatible target sublanguage inherits the lock and must contain both its support and all omitted points. The additional point ensures that sublanguage has a valid full-support PMF.

Theorem 3.8 uses support stability essentially. The stronger semantic no-rate lemma does not need MOP; the canonical wrapper retains source pointwise decidable MOP and does not infer uniformity. The family hypothesis is failure of semantic Angluin ConditionTwo, not merely ordinary effective non-identifiability.

NoApproximateBreadthRate gives one fixed valid target distribution with positive limsup failure and excludes every vanishing natural-domain rate and real-domain rate with positive distribution-dependent horizontal and vertical scales. No uniform numerical constant such as one half is asserted.

The alternative finite-sample proof does not duplicate source Lemmas 7.5--7.6 or construct an infinite-IID stream transfer. The locking prefix, omission set, and tell-tale are classical proof witnesses, without an effective construction or randomized online derandomization claim.
Core.SubsetOracle is an exact Boolean indexed-language inclusion interface, separate from the standing membership oracle. Semantic oracle correctness does not imply ordinary computability.

Proposition 3.10 uses one fixed TruthTableProgram. At sample length n it considers zero-based indices below n, asks membership for observed points and all earlier-index subset comparisons, and returns the last critical index. Query formation is primitive recursive and postprocessing is computable.

The target tell-tale together with positive counterexamples to earlier languages not containing the target is a finite witness. Once observed and n is at least the target index plus one, the target is critical and every later critical candidate denotes the same target. The witness is used only in the proof, not by the program.

Lemma 8.1 gives error at most D exp(-c n) for all sample sizes, with positive constants depending on the valid target distribution. This is the source exponential rate class under its allowed rescalings, not a universal coefficient-one bound.

The same subsetIdentifier is uniformly ordinarily Computable when membership and inclusion queries are both computable. No computable inclusion oracle or tell-tale procedure is inferred from nonuniform ConditionTwo alone.

The last-critical rule matches the Appendix B.1 construction for statistical language prediction, with default index zero when no critical candidate exists. Duplicate target indices may vary; fixed-index online postprocessing and Appendix B.2 breadth generation are not claimed as covered.

Theorem 3.13 reuses Gold InformantDatum and InformantCompatible. ValidLabeledDistribution is proved equivalent to full support of the domain marginal and deterministic correct labels; the loss compares denoted languages, permitting duplicate indices.

Theorem 3.13 uses a fixed bounded least-consistent membership-only learner: at sample length n, test indices below n against all observed labels, returning the least consistent index or zero. Computable membership gives ordinary uniform computation. Finite separating labels are classical proof witnesses and are not algorithm inputs.

The labeled upper bound is D exp(-c n) for every sample size, with positive distribution-dependent constants and no source batching estimator. The labeled lower bound gives one fixed valid law with error at least exp(-2n) infinitely often for every randomized kernel under source NontrivialCollection. Correct-label pushforwards of a full-support heavy-atom marginal ensure validity on positive and negative points, including empty complements.

OnlineComputation reuses breadthIdentifier and proves syntactic fixed-index convergence from eventual completed-support equality. The boundedUnambiguousIdentifier implements finite positive consistency and prefix coverage tests and stabilizes to the least target index. Both are ordinarily computable under computable family membership and uniform support membership.

Theorem 3.5 has two actual PMF generators: identifiedBreadth deletes the sample; identifiedRepeatingBreadth keeps the whole conjectured language. Seeded samplers, OracleMOP, conditional ordinary pointwise MOP, and conditional uniform sampler/MOP certificates are proved. No arbitrary semantic identifier is declared ordinarily computable.

The effective_identification_iff_fresh_breadth and repeating biconditionals reuse P00A EffectiveInferrable and require HasComputableSampler plus UniformDecidableMOP on the generator side. Effective non-identifiability corollaries for 3.7/3.9 likewise require uniform MOP. These separate results do not identify ConditionOne with ConditionTwo or extract a uniform decider from pointwise existence.
gaps: Proposition A.1; Theorem B.1; and Corollary B.2 have no claim-covering Lean theorem.

A compiler from literal randomized Turing-machine syntax, a universal validity/totality checker for arbitrary machine descriptions, and general undecidability reductions remain outside the encoded operational model. The new online wrappers cover the PMF/MOP interfaces, and the effective corollaries use Mathlib Computable functions and seeded samplers. A compiler from arbitrary literal randomized TM syntax is not required by the stronger negative bounds and is not supplied.

The source's infinite-IID and generic black-box boosting proofs are not duplicated: the full Theorem 3.1 follows by a stronger explicit-learner upper bound and a direct finite-sample Baire obstruction. Theorem 3.13 likewise uses a direct finite-separator proof rather than separately formalizing source Proposition 8.3 and Lemma 8.4; their generic black-box statements have no independent endpoints.

The positive online PMF theorem uses infinite candidate languages, as in the existing generation model; finite exhausted targets are not assigned an empty PMF. The legacy general support-set theorem remains available. No ordinary effective non-identifiability result under merely pointwise MOP is inferred from the new uniform-MOP corollaries.

The literal reversed unambiguous-loss objective is not validated; Theorem 3.6 uses the intended failure loss with an explicit complement theorem. A named human faithfulness audit of this correction and of the semantic/non-effective classifier scope remains pending.
No named human correspondence audit exists for P03.
The post-Theorem-3.2 remark about generating infinitely many new outputs from a fixed training sample is not asserted by the single-output facade; both bounds of the numbered theorem are proved.

Source Proposition 7.2 and Lemmas 7.3--7.6 remain unformalized as separate claims; the alternative proofs of Theorems 3.6 and 3.8 need no infinite-IID stream transfer or randomized online derandomization.

The Proposition 3.10 last-critical program and finite-witness language-correctness proof now implement the shared Appendix B.1 construction, but no fixed-index online identification endpoint or Appendix B.2 breadth generator is asserted.

audit_refs.scope: Tracked source-to-Lean map for online PMF/MOP results, statistical identification, generation, breadth, and unambiguous-generation results, proof repairs, and remaining computability and universal-rate gaps; not a named human audit.

Project-wide selected axiom checks include the P03 statistical theorems, sampler/MOP computation certificates, and online semantic declarations; these checks do not establish human source correspondence.

claims.title: Definitions 5--9 fix semantic support access, exact stability, and two breadth relaxations
claims.statement_summary: A support generator exposes its raw support and an extensionally exact Boolean membership answer after each finite history. Along every exact positive presentation, stability means that all sufficiently late raw supports are exactly equal; unambiguous generation means that every sufficiently late support has strictly smaller extended-cardinality symmetric difference from the target than from every extensionally distinct indexed language; and approximate breadth means eventual target containment with only finitely many omitted target elements.

source_assessment.notes: Lean records the probability-free online support semantics, not the statistical rate theorems and not randomized Turing-machine code. SupportGenerator.query is extensionally correct for its supplied support but does not certify the source's code-level MOP decidability. FreshBreadthInLimit and RepeatingBreadthInLimit remain separate helpers for the fresh-versus-whole-target convention around Theorem 3.5; neither is silently folded into Definitions 7--9. Statistical DecidableMOP now records Definition 6's pointwise computable-decider quantifiers, separately from the stronger uniform interface and certified oracle programs. Arbitrary randomized Turing-machine descriptions remain outside this model.

formalization.notes: Four online semantic components retain their canonical endpoints. DecidableMOP additionally records pointwise ordinary computable support deciders; UniformDecidableMOP and OracleMOP remain separate interfaces. The constructed statistical generators have certified samplers and support programs, but arbitrary randomized Turing-machine descriptions and general code-level MOP arguments are not encoded. The online stability/unambiguity/approximate-breadth meanings are unchanged.

components.summary: After each finite history the generator supplies a raw support set and a Boolean query that is true exactly on that support.
The fully general MOP interface from descriptions of arbitrary randomized Turing machines is not encoded.
On every exact target presentation, every pair of sufficiently late raw support sets is extensionally equal.
Every sufficiently late support is strictly closer in extended-cardinality symmetric difference to the target than to every extensionally different indexed language.
Every sufficiently late support is contained in the target and omits only finitely many target elements.
For each finite training sample there exists a total Computable Boolean function that decides membership in the trained PMF support, with no uniformity in the sample inferred.

lean_links.notes: The query_spec field gives exact extensional answers but is not a Turing-computability certificate for Definitions 5--6.
The stabilization time may depend on the target and presentation; completedSupport is not used.
UnambiguousAt compares Set.encard values for every i with C i != C z; it does not merely compare different indices or finite cardinalities.
ApproximateBreadthAt is exactly S subset K and (K minus S).Finite; it is neither freshness nor a density-one condition.
Captures Definition 6's pointwise quantifier order. It is distinct from one uniform computable sample/query decider and does not encode arbitrary machine descriptions.

relations.notes: Theorem 3.5 uses the same semantic support-oracle interface but keeps fresh and repetition-allowing breadth as separate conventions.
Theorem 3.7 rules out the conjunction of the stability and unambiguity predicates for non-identifiable families.
Theorem 3.9 rules out the conjunction of stability and approximate breadth for non-identifiable families.

audit_refs.scope: Maps Definitions 5--9 to the probability-free Lean interfaces and records the missing computability certificate and fresh-versus-repeating support convention.
Generated declaration-existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for the five linked definition endpoints.

claims.title: Positive-only identification has an almost-exponential-or-no-rate dichotomy
claims.statement_summary: For every nontrivial countable language collection under positive IID data, exactly one alternative holds: if Angluin's condition holds, then every sublinear exponent g admits identification rate exp(-g(n)) and no learner is faster than exponential; otherwise the collection admits no identification rate.

source_assessment.notes: The theorem is interpreted in Definition 11's membership/tell-tale-enumeration oracle model. Its g=o(n) quantifier is restricted to nonnegative divergent exponents, as Definition 13 requires a [0,1]-valued rate tending to zero. Lean proves the stronger exponential upper bound for the explicit Angluin stage learner and uses horizontal rate scale one; the no-rate proof is an independent Baire argument. Ordinary computability is certified separately under effective ConditionOne, without identifying it with nonuniform ConditionTwo. No named human correspondence audit has yet confirmed these qualifications.

formalization.notes: All mathematical alternatives and the source-oracle computation witness are proved. The explicit stage learner has finite witnesses, hence exponential error decay and every admissible almost-exponential rate with one fixed learner. Failure of finite tell-tales yields a fixed valid distribution with limsup error at least one half for every randomized learner. Query formation is primitive recursive and postprocessing is Computable, using only bounded prefixes of the supplied membership/tell-tale oracles. The stronger proof avoids assuming the attributed Angluin-1988 theorem or the source's infinite-IID boosting machinery.

components.summary: Every randomized PMF learner has a fixed target and valid distribution with error at least exp(-2n) infinitely often.

Angluin finite tell-tales yield every admissible almost-exponential rate; the explicit stage learner actually has an exponential upper rate with the learner fixed before the exponent and distribution.
Failure of finite tell-tales yields, for every randomized learner, one fixed valid distribution with limsup error at least one half, hence no identification rate.

The two alternatives are exclusive, the positive alternative is equivalent to Angluin condition, and a certified truth-table learner realizes the positive branch under membership and tell-tale-enumeration access.

lean_links.notes: Canonical full wrapper. The positive branch includes a certified finite-query program and a stronger exponential upper bound; admissible exponents are nonnegative, divergent, and sublinear. The no-rate branch applies to all randomized PMF kernels. The direct Baire proof uses no unproved statistical theorem hypothesis.

relations.notes: The learnable branch uses the effective positive-data characterization as its online qualitative boundary.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for the complete Theorem 3.1 oracle-relative wrapper; this is not a named human correspondence audit.

claims.title: Consistent generation has an exponential universal rate
claims.statement_summary: Every countable indexed collection of infinite languages admits consistent fresh generation at rate exp(-n), while every randomized generator has a matching exponential lower bound infinitely often under one fixed valid distribution when the collection is nontrivial for generation.

source_assessment.notes: The infinitude premise is explicit in the source generation discussion on page 2 and is used in Lemma 5.10's proof. Lean states it through OracleFamily.infinite'. The statistical loss is equation (5), without Definition 12's exhausted-finite-target exception. The public computation witness is a stateless variant of finite-critical KM search; the original P01 stateful machine separately receives the finite-witness and exponential-rate proofs. These source qualifications have not received a named human correspondence audit.

formalization.notes: Both bounds of the numbered theorem are proved in the explicit infinite-language membership-oracle model. Lemma 5.11 reuses IID finite coverage; Lemma 5.13 strengthens P01's actual finite-query machine. The stateless certified witness searches only membership tables and has proved termination. The randomized lower proof selects a hard target before choosing a full-support distribution and lower-bounding its hard sample atoms. No tell-tale or subset oracle, distribution advice, or unproved rate hypothesis is used.

components.summary: One fixed membership-only certified generator has error at most D exp(-c n) for every valid target distribution and every sample size, with positive distribution-dependent constants.
For every randomized generator on a generation-nontrivial family, one fixed target and valid distribution have error at least D exp(-c n) infinitely often.
Primitive recursive finite query stages and a computable postprocessor, with successful-stage termination proved using P01 KM rounds; computable uniform membership yields a Computable learner.

lean_links.notes: Canonical full wrapper in the source's infinite-language generation regime. The algorithm is fixed before the target distribution, and generation-specific nontriviality is required only for the lower bound. No complexity bound or post-theorem infinite-output strengthening is asserted.

relations.notes: The source lifts qualitative online generation to a statistical exponential-rate guarantee, but the P01 result is not counted as P03 coverage.

audit_refs.scope: Generated declaration existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for full Theorem 3.2; not a human correspondence audit.

claims.title: Statistical breadth separates identifiable and non-identifiable collections
claims.statement_summary: For nontrivial countable collections that are not identifiable in the limit, no generator with decidable support-membership problem achieves breadth at any rate, although such a generator achieves consistent generation without breadth at exponential rate and no generator is faster; for identifiable collections, decidable-MOP breadth is achievable at every almost-exponential rate, again with the exponential consistency lower bound.

source_assessment.notes: The theorem is interpreted in the infinite-language generation regime and Theorem 3.1's explicit membership/tell-tale-oracle model. Definition 6 has pointwise MOP quantifiers, whereas the printed reduction describes a uniform support query; Lean distinguishes these interfaces and uses a stronger semantic necessity theorem to prove the negative result for the pointwise class without a uniformization assumption. The positive sampler is a geometric-seed upward search rather than rejection sampling. Ordinary uniform sampler/MOP certificates require computable membership and tell-tale enumeration and are separately proved under effective ConditionOne. Fresh support is used throughout; Remark 2's general repetition conversion is not asserted. No named human correspondence audit has confirmed these qualifications.

formalization.notes: The complete statistical separation and optimality clauses are proved in the explicit infinite-language oracle model. The negative proof uses a bounded finite-label identifier and eventual error domination. Positive breadth follows from the actual Theorem 3.1 identifier and a certified exact-support sampler. The consistent branch and randomized lower bound reuse Theorem 3.2. Oracle-relative and ordinary effective claims are separate; no computable training procedure is inferred from bare semantic identifiability.

components.summary: Every generator with pointwise decidable MOP on a non-identifiable family has positive limsup breadth error under one fixed valid distribution; a stronger lemma gives a one-half bound for all semantic PMF generators.
The Theorem 3.2 generator has pointwise decidable MOP and optimal exponential consistency rates; its seeded sampler is ordinarily computable under computable membership.
